_about: SQL playground exercises. Each exercise's expected result is computed by running its solution on the sample database, so the visitor's result is compared with that.
setup: CREATE TABLE students (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, major TEXT NOT NULL, year INTEGER NOT NULL, city TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE courses (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, credits INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE enrollments (student_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES students(id), course_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES courses(id), term TEXT NOT NULL, grade INTEGER);

INSERT INTO courses VALUES (101,'Intro to Programming','CS',3),(102,'Databases','CS',3),(103,'Computer Networks','ECE',4),(104,'Linear Algebra','MATH',3),(105,'Security Basics','ECE',3),(106,'Technical Writing','ENGL',2);

exercises.question: Show the name and major of every student.
exercises.hint: List the columns you want after SELECT, then the table after FROM.
exercises.solution: SELECT name, major FROM students;
exercises.readme: 1. SELECT / FROM: Show the name and major of every student.

exercises.question: Show the title and number of credits of every course.
exercises.hint: Same pattern: SELECT column1, column2 FROM table.
exercises.solution: SELECT title, credits FROM courses;
exercises.readme: 2. SELECT / FROM: Show the title and number of credits of every course.

exercises.question: Show every column of the enrollments table.
exercises.hint: * means "all columns".
exercises.solution: SELECT * FROM enrollments;
exercises.readme: 3. SELECT / FROM: Show every column of the enrollments table.

exercises.question: Find the names of students who live in Victoria.
exercises.hint: Text values go in single quotes: WHERE city = '...'.
exercises.solution: SELECT name FROM students WHERE city = 'Victoria';
exercises.readme: 4. WHERE: Find the names of students who live in Victoria.

exercises.question: Find enrollments with a grade of 85 or higher. Show student_id, course_id, and grade.
exercises.hint: Use >= for "or higher".
exercises.solution: SELECT student_id, course_id, grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade >= 85;
exercises.readme: 5. WHERE: Find enrollments with a grade of 85 or higher. Show student_id, course_id, and grade.

exercises.question: Find enrollments that don't have a grade yet. Show student_id and course_id.
exercises.hint: grade = NULL never matches anything. NULL needs a special check: IS NULL.
exercises.solution: SELECT student_id, course_id FROM enrollments WHERE grade IS NULL;
exercises.readme: 6. WHERE: Find enrollments that don't have a grade yet. Show student_id and course_id.

exercises.question: List every student's name, year, and city, with the highest year first. For students in the same year, sort by city A–Z, and then by name A–Z.
exercises.hint: You can sort by several columns: ORDER BY col1 DESC, col2, col3. Later columns only break ties.
exercises.solution: SELECT name, year, city FROM students ORDER BY year DESC, city ASC, name ASC;
exercises.readme: 7. ORDER BY: List every student's name, year, and city, with the highest year first. For students in the same year, sort by city A–Z, and then by name A–Z.

exercises.question: List course titles and credits, from the most credits to the fewest. For courses with the same credits, sort titles A–Z.
exercises.hint: DESC means largest first; ASC (the default) means smallest first.
exercises.solution: SELECT title, credits FROM courses ORDER BY credits DESC, title;
exercises.readme: 8. ORDER BY: List course titles and credits, from the most credits to the fewest. For courses with the same credits, sort titles A–Z.

exercises.question: Show the 3 highest grades (student_id, course_id, grade), highest first.
exercises.hint: Sort, then keep only the first rows with LIMIT.
exercises.solution: SELECT student_id, course_id, grade FROM enrollments ORDER BY grade DESC LIMIT 3;
exercises.readme: 9. ORDER BY: Show the 3 highest grades (student_id, course_id, grade), highest first.

exercises.question: How many students are there?
exercises.hint: COUNT(*) counts rows.
exercises.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students;
exercises.readme: 10. COUNT / SUM: How many students are there?

exercises.question: What is the total number of credits across all courses?
exercises.hint: SUM(column) adds up a column.
exercises.solution: SELECT SUM(credits) FROM courses;
exercises.readme: 11. COUNT / SUM: What is the total number of credits across all courses?

exercises.question: How many enrollments have a grade? (Don't count the ones without a grade.)
exercises.hint: COUNT(*) counts every row, but COUNT(column) skips NULL values.
exercises.solution: SELECT COUNT(grade) FROM enrollments;
exercises.readme: 12. COUNT / SUM: How many enrollments have a grade? (Don't count the ones without a grade.)

exercises.question: How many students are in each major? Show the major and the count.
exercises.hint: GROUP BY major makes one group per major; COUNT(*) then counts each group.
exercises.solution: SELECT major, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY major;
exercises.readme: 13. GROUP BY: How many students are in each major? Show the major and the count.

exercises.question: How many students are enrolled in each course? Show course_id and the count.
exercises.hint: Group the enrollments by course_id.
exercises.solution: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;
exercises.readme: 14. GROUP BY: How many students are enrolled in each course? Show course_id and the count.

exercises.question: What is the highest grade in each term? Show term and the highest grade.
exercises.hint: MAX(column) works per group, just like COUNT and SUM.
exercises.solution: SELECT term, MAX(grade) FROM enrollments GROUP BY term;
exercises.readme: 15. GROUP BY: What is the highest grade in each term? Show term and the highest grade.

exercises.question: List every student's name with the course_id of each of their enrollments. Students with no enrollments must still appear, with NULL as the course_id.
exercises.hint: A LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table, even if nothing matches on the right.
exercises.solution: SELECT s.name, e.course_id FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id;
exercises.readme: 16. LEFT JOIN: List every student's name with the course_id of each of their enrollments. Students with no enrollments must still appear, with NULL as the course_id.

exercises.question: List every course title with how many enrollments it has. Courses with no enrollments should show 0.
exercises.hint: COUNT(*) would count 1 for an unmatched row. COUNT(e.student_id) skips the NULLs, so empty courses get 0.
exercises.solution: SELECT c.title, COUNT(e.student_id) FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.title;
exercises.readme: 17. LEFT JOIN: List every course title with how many enrollments it has. Courses with no enrollments should show 0.

exercises.question: Find the names of students who aren't enrolled in any course.
exercises.hint: LEFT JOIN, then keep only the rows where the right side found no match (it's NULL).
exercises.solution: SELECT s.name FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id WHERE e.student_id IS NULL;
exercises.readme: 18. LEFT JOIN: Find the names of students who aren't enrolled in any course.

exercises.question: Which majors have more than 2 students? Show the major and the count.
exercises.hint: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after grouping.
exercises.solution: SELECT major, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY major HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;
exercises.readme: 19. HAVING: Which majors have more than 2 students? Show the major and the count.

exercises.question: Which students are enrolled in at least 3 courses? Show student_id and the number of courses.
exercises.hint: Group by student_id, then keep groups with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
exercises.solution: SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;
exercises.readme: 20. HAVING: Which students are enrolled in at least 3 courses? Show student_id and the number of courses.

exercises.question: Which courses have an average grade above 80? Show course_id and the average rounded to 1 decimal place.
exercises.hint: AVG ignores NULL grades. Use ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) and put the condition in HAVING.
exercises.solution: SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id HAVING AVG(grade) > 80;
exercises.readme: 21. HAVING: Which courses have an average grade above 80? Show course_id and the average rounded to 1 decimal place.

exercises.question: Using an INNER JOIN, list each student's name with the title of each course they're enrolled in.
exercises.hint: You need two joins: students → enrollments → courses.
exercises.solution: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id;
exercises.readme: 22. INNER vs LEFT JOIN: Using an INNER JOIN, list each student's name with the title of each course they're enrolled in.

exercises.question: Now start from courses and LEFT JOIN to enrollments: list every course title with the student_id of each enrollment (NULL if a course has none).
exercises.hint: With a LEFT JOIN, a course with no enrollments still shows up once, with NULL.
exercises.solution: SELECT c.title, e.student_id FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id;
exercises.readme: 23. INNER vs LEFT JOIN: Now start from courses and LEFT JOIN to enrollments: list every course title with the student_id of each enrollment (NULL if a course has none).

exercises.question: How many rows does students INNER JOIN enrollments return, and how many does students LEFT JOIN enrollments return? Return one row with two columns: inner_rows and left_rows.
exercises.hint: You can put a whole query in parentheses as a value: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ...) AS inner_rows, (...) AS left_rows;
exercises.solution: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id) AS inner_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id) AS left_rows;
exercises.readme: 24. INNER vs LEFT JOIN: How many rows does students INNER JOIN enrollments return, and how many does students LEFT JOIN enrollments return? Return one row with two columns: inner_rows and left_rows.

exercises.question: Using a subquery with IN, find the names of students enrolled in course 105.
exercises.hint: WHERE id IN (SELECT student_id FROM enrollments WHERE ...).
exercises.solution: SELECT name FROM students WHERE id IN (SELECT student_id FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 105);
exercises.readme: 25. Subqueries: Using a subquery with IN, find the names of students enrolled in course 105.

exercises.question: Find enrollments whose grade is higher than the average of all grades. Show student_id, course_id, and grade.
exercises.hint: Compare each grade with (SELECT AVG(grade) FROM enrollments).
exercises.solution: SELECT student_id, course_id, grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade > (SELECT AVG(grade) FROM enrollments);
exercises.readme: 26. Subqueries: Find enrollments whose grade is higher than the average of all grades. Show student_id, course_id, and grade.

exercises.question: Find the title of the course (or courses) with the most credits.
exercises.hint: Find the maximum with a subquery, then match it: WHERE credits = (SELECT MAX(credits) FROM courses).
exercises.solution: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE credits = (SELECT MAX(credits) FROM courses);
exercises.readme: 27. Subqueries: Find the title of the course (or courses) with the most credits.

exercises.question: For each enrollment, show student_id, course_id, and a column called result: 'in progress' if there's no grade, 'pass' if the grade is 60 or more, and 'fail' otherwise.
exercises.hint: Check for NULL first. CASE WHEN ... THEN ... WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END.
exercises.solution: SELECT student_id, course_id, CASE WHEN grade IS NULL THEN 'in progress' WHEN grade >= 60 THEN 'pass' ELSE 'fail' END AS result FROM enrollments;
exercises.readme: 28. CASE WHEN: For each enrollment, show student_id, course_id, and a column called result: 'in progress' if there's no grade, 'pass' if the grade is 60 or more, and 'fail' otherwise.

exercises.question: Label each course as 'light' (fewer than 3 credits), 'normal' (exactly 3), or 'heavy' (more than 3). Show title and the label.
exercises.hint: CASE is checked from top to bottom, and the first true condition wins.
exercises.solution: SELECT title, CASE WHEN credits < 3 THEN 'light' WHEN credits = 3 THEN 'normal' ELSE 'heavy' END AS label FROM courses;
exercises.readme: 29. CASE WHEN: Label each course as 'light' (fewer than 3 credits), 'normal' (exactly 3), or 'heavy' (more than 3). Show title and the label.

exercises.question: In one query, count how many enrollments are passing (grade 60 or more) and how many are failing (grade below 60). Return two columns: passing and failing. Enrollments without a grade count as neither.
exercises.hint: SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts the rows where the condition is true.
exercises.solution: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN grade >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passing, SUM(CASE WHEN grade < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failing FROM enrollments;
exercises.readme: 30. CASE WHEN: In one query, count how many enrollments are passing (grade 60 or more) and how many are failing (grade below 60). Return two columns: passing and failing. Enrollments without a grade count as neither.
